discovery: Theoretical prediction and establishment of altermagnetism as a third fundamental class of collinear magnetic order

nominees.name: Tomas Jungwirth
nominees.affiliation: Institute of Physics, Czech Academy of Sciences, Prague, and University of Nottingham

nominees.name: Libor Šmejkal
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems, Dresden, and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz

subfield: Condensed matter physics: magnetism and spintronics
motivation: For nearly a century magnetic order was divided into ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. Using spin-group symmetry analysis, Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth showed that a third class exists. In altermagnets, compensated collinear moments on sublattices related by rotations rather than translations or inversion give zero net magnetization. Yet the electronic bands are strongly spin-split, with alternating d-, g- or i-wave symmetry. This is a general organizing principle, rooted in symmetry, that changes how we classify broken-symmetry phases. It predicts an anomalous Hall effect, spin-polarized currents and unconventional superconducting proximity effects without stray fields. Their prediction was later confirmed experimentally: spin-resolved photoemission in 2024 directly observed altermagnetic band splitting in MnTe and CrSb, and imaging resolved altermagnetic domains. Jungwirth's earlier pioneering of antiferromagnetic spintronics laid the groundwork. The field now spans many materials and offers a fast, robust platform for spintronics.
